per_stage_summary.label: Delivery: POD, Last-Leg Verification & Physical Security

gate_reasoning: Global Low% is 71.3% of non-speculative claims (283 of 397), which exceeds the >70% re-run-recommended threshold. Even using all 407 claims as denominator (69.5%), the corpus is barely within the ship-with-flag band. Two of six stages (Stage 2 and Stage 5) individually scored re-run-recommended in per-stage validation. Stage 5 (Delivery) reached 82.2% Low driven by 31 vendor-marketing override claims and 17 aggregator auto-downgrade hits — the highest single-stage Low% in the corpus. Stage 4 (Control Tower, 69.8%) and Stage 6 (Post-Incident, 72.2%) each crossed 70% on their non-speculative counts. The dominant failure modes corpus-wide are vendor-marketing override (~102 claims), aggregator market-research auto-downgrade (~53 claims), and single-trade-source override (~57 claims). DR pass-3 refinements were applied across all stages and reduced Low% 5-10 points from pre-DR baselines, but were insufficient to bring the corpus below the re-run threshold. Recommendation: targeted deep-research on Stage 5 pain points (PP5.1 damage rate, PP5.2 theft cost, PP5.3 escort cost) and Stage 2 routing/spot-market claims before final ship.

override_triggers_cross_stage.note: Single largest override. Vendor capability/coverage/market-share claims sourced from same vendor's marketing surface (project44.com, fourkites.com, shippeo.com, samsara.com, motive.com, etc). Stage 5 worst (31 claims), Stage 4 second (21 claims).
Operating cost figures and frequency claims sourced only from FreightWaves, JOC, The Loadstar, or single-outlet trade press. Stage 2 worst (14 claims), Stage 5 second (14 claims).

Market sizing claims from MarketsandMarkets, Mordor Intelligence, Grand View Research, GMInsights, DataIntelo, Fortune Business Insights, ResearchAndMarkets. Stage 5 worst (17 claims), Stage 6 second (9 claims), Stage 4 third (9 claims).

Claims tagged [ASSUMED-N] in source drafts, indicating no verifiable citation. Stage 5 worst (15 claims). Includes WH5 parametric insurance figures dropped in DR refinements, and control-tower workflow metrics (34 manual updates / 6 platforms; 25 emails / 8 roles).

Funding round sizes, partnership announcements, capability launches sourced from PR Newswire / BusinessWire / GlobeNewswire without corroborating Form D or 10-K. Stage 6 worst (7 claims), Stage 3 second (6 claims).
Multiple trade sources tracing to same paywalled primary (Gartner, Forrester, IDC) — counted as 1 or 0 verifiable sources depending on whether underlying primary is accessible.
APAC-regional market sizing or penetration figure used as proxy for country-specific SEA need. Flags: Geography mismatch. All such claims capped at Medium.

PDF-binary or anti-bot response prevented verbatim quote extraction for High-tier claims. Affects Transporeon/Trimble filing, TT Club 2024 Annual Report PDF, and Parsyl Lloyd's syndicate filings. Evidence quote gaps recorded.

Sources >3 years old or market data >2 years old without cross-validation to recent source. Includes World Bank LPI 2013 Indonesia logistics cost (mitigated by Bappenas/BPS ANTARA 2023 cross-validation in Stages 1 and 2).
Multiple URLs from same publication family cited as independent sources. Includes multiple FreightWaves articles for double-brokering cost (Stage 2) and multiple TT Club press releases (Stage 6).

top_10_cross_stage_recurring_sources.publisher: TT Club / BSI Cargo Theft Report 2024
top_10_cross_stage_recurring_sources.note: Corpus anchor for cargo theft frequency and cost data globally and SEA. TT Club 2024 Annual Report ($283.1M GWP) provides insurance market sizing; BSI/TT Club joint report provides theft intelligence.
Primary anchor for US cargo theft dollar values ($455M reported 2024, $332M 2023) and freight fraud figures. Cited across vendor procurement, dispatch, in-transit, delivery, and claims stages.
Anchor for SEA logistics performance benchmarking — Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia LPI scores. Cross-cited across four stages for logistics cost and infrastructure gap claims.
FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center public service announcement April 2026 on freight fraud. Used alongside Verisk CargoNet to corroborate double-brokering/identity-theft cost figures.

Supply Chain Resilience Jan 2024 report cited for $65-95B blind handoff opportunity (US-only scope confirmed verbatim). Also cited in Stage 4 and Stage 6 for supply-chain visibility and insurance market evolution claims.

US Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration SAFER Web database. Anchor for carrier onboarding compliance and broker registration data. Limited geographic scope (US-only) flagged for SEA applicability.

Indonesian government sources: Bappenas (National Development Planning Agency) and BPS (Central Statistics Agency) via ANTARA newswire. Used for Indonesia logistics cost as % of GDP (23.27%), the highest in the corpus for a specific SEA country.
Annual 3PL study providing shipper-reported satisfaction data on carrier API completion, visibility tool adoption, and control-tower investment intentions. Named-firm authored report.

dr_refinements_applied_note: Pass-3 deep-research refinements were applied across all 6 stages prior to this final cross-stage validation. Key upgrades: (1) Verisk CargoNet upgraded from Tier-9 Travelers citation to primary-association across Stages 1, 2, 5, 6; (2) Berg Insight SEA telematics upgraded from aggregator-press-release to specialist analyst (Stage 3); (3) World Bank + Bappenas/BPS cross-validation of Indonesia logistics cost (Stages 1, 2); (4) Vesttoo fraud figure reconciled to court-verified $3.4B (Stage 6); (5) WH5 parametric cluster dropped (all MarketGrowthReports.com — Stage 6); (6) FourKites control-tower metrics tagged [ASSUMED-9] (Stage 4); (7) Montgomery v. Caribe SCOTUS May 2026 added as new pain point (Stage 1). Despite these refinements, global Low% remains at 71.3% (non-speculative), above the re-run threshold, driven primarily by vendor-marketing, aggregator, and single-trade-source overrides on vendor capability and market-sizing claims across all stages.
